messages:
Jordan (acme-app): hey @support, hitting a weird one — our embedded iframe loses session after switching browser tabs. users auth via SSO + MFA, complete the flow, then if they switch away and back the iframe shows the login button again. looks like a reauth loop. no server errors, just the iframe appears unauthenticated.
Emma (support): thanks Jordan — can you share browser version, SDK version, and quick repro steps? any console logs or network traces would help.
Jordan (acme-app): repro steps below, happening in Chrome 118 on macOS (non-incognito). SDK version: redwood-embed v0.9.2.
```
1) Open app with embedded iframe to https://app.acme/canvas
2) Login via corporate SSO, complete MFA (Okta + push)
3) Iframe shows authenticated content
4) Open new tab, visit gmail briefly, switch back
5) Iframe now shows sign-in button, clicking it triggers SSO again and it loops
```
Console shows: `Set-Cookie "sid" was blocked because it had the "SameSite=None" attribute but was set from a third-party context.` and `Failed to execute 'postMessage' on 'DOMWindow': The target origin provided ('https://embed.redwood.ai') does not match the recipient window's origin.`
Emma (support): hmm, that cookie-block message suggests browser is treating the iframe as third-party. Are you loading the iframe cross-origin? Is the host and embed on different domains?
Jordan (acme-app): yes host: https://app.acme, embed src: https://embed.redwood.ai. We rely on an httponly session cookie `sid` for iframe auth, and a top-level oauth token for top-level redirects. Works in same-tab flows, only breaks after tab switching.
Sam (devex): tagging in — we've seen similar symptoms when Chrome partitions third-party cookies or when Storage Access API isn't granted. Two quick asks: can you test with `--disable-features=PartitionedCookies` (dev flag) and confirm? Also try latest embed v0.9.6 (we added a storage fallback).
Maria (eng-sre): +1. Also need to confirm whether the idp does any top-level redirect after MFA that could cause the iframe's postMessage origin to change. The `postMessage` mismatch looks like the embed window was replaced by a redirect to the idp domain and then replaced back, changing nested frame origins. Can you capture network waterfall for the login flow?
Jordan (acme-app): captured HAR attached (link: https://acme.s3/har/har-1723456789.har) — key snippet: after MFA the idp does a top-level redirect then returns to `https://app.acme/return` which in turn reloads the iframe src to `https://embed.redwood.ai/auth/callback?token=...`. We see `Set-Cookie` header from embed response but Chrome blocks it: `Set-Cookie: sid=abcd; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=None; HttpOnly`.
deploy-bot: INC-7892 created (priority P2) — incident ticket created for embed auth flakes.
Emma (support): ok. For a short-term workaround you can: 1) switch the embed to open the MFA/SSO flow in a top-level popup instead of inside the iframe OR 2) exchange the token via a top-level redirect that stores a first-party cookie on app.acme and then postMessage the session to the iframe. Which would you prefer to try? :thinking_face:
Jordan (acme-app): try popup first — less app changes. Any code sample?
Sam (devex): here's a minimal popup flow we recommend — open a top-level window for the idp and on success postMessage the result back to the parent which then forwards to the iframe.
```
const popup = window.open(idpUrl, 'idp', 'width=600,height=700');
window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
  if (e.origin !== 'https://app.acme') return;
  const payload = e.data; // { token }
  // forward to iframe
  iframe.contentWindow.postMessage(payload, 'https://embed.redwood.ai');
});
```
Jordan (acme-app): thanks — I'll try.
Maria (eng-sre): longer-term, platform note: Chrome's cookie partitioning and ITP have increased blocking of cross-site cookies after background tabing, especially when the idp issues a top-level redirect. We recommend moving session ownership to top-level host or using Storage Access API to request access from within the iframe. Another option is SameParty if your domains are eligible.
Kevin (platform): also flagging an SDK improvement — we'll add a more robust handshake and token-refresh fallback in the next embed release (v0.9.8). Plan: if cookie missing after focus event, try postMessage token refresh to parent, then retry load. I'll open a release task.
Emma (support): Maria, can you add diagnostic checklist for engineering: 1) confirm cookie presence in Network (Set-Cookie) and Application->Cookies before/after tab switch; 2) capture postMessage origin history; 3) test with third-party cookie blocking flags; 4) test popup vs top-level redirect.
Maria (eng-sre): added to INC-7892 checklist, assigned to eng-sre.
Jordan (acme-app): ran popup flow — MFA popup works and iframe gets token via postMessage, no loop. ✅ Popup is a fine short-term fix. We'll test with customers who hit the issue.
Sam (devex): great. We'll prioritize v0.9.8 with fallback and document guidance about SSO+MFA for embeds in the docs (link: https://docs.redwood.ai/embed-auth).
Jordan (acme-app): thanks everyone, appreciate the quick help. I'll keep the ticket updated if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
Emma (support): thanks Jordan — marking as escalated, will follow through release and docs updates.
